sections.h2: West Des Moines at a glance
sections.html:
West Des Moines is a western suburb of Des Moines in central Iowa. Most of the city lies in Polk County, parts extend into Dallas County, and small portions reach into Warren and Madison counties. In 2020 the census found 68,723 residents, which put it sixth among Iowa cities and second in the Des Moines metro. An estimate for July 1, 2025 reads 74,224.

sections.h2: From Valley Junction to a big suburb
sections.html:
The town was incorporated as Valley Junction on October 9, 1893, and kept that name until January 1, 1938, once voters backed the switch to West Des Moines on December 7, 1937. The Rock Island railroad depot and shops shaped the early town.

The city then grew by annexation: Clover Hills in 1950, Ashawa in 1957, Commerce in 1960 and land in Warren County in 2005. That patchwork means house age, lot size and street layout vary widely depending on the neighborhood.

The old business district, Historic Valley Junction, earned a National Register of Historic Places listing on October 11, 2017. The listing covers about 12 acres and 72 resources, of which 53 are contributing buildings, mostly one and two story brick.

Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $309,000 for 2020 to 2024, and 57.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied, leaving roughly 43 percent of households as renters. Typical gross rent is $1,237 and household income $86,594, with 2.19 people per household.

Those are citywide middles, and one house may land well above or below them.

The biggest employer is Wells Fargo Home Mortgage and Credit Services at about 9,000 workers. Insurers and financial firms dominate beyond that, including Athene, FBL Financial Group, American Equity and Sammons Financial Group. Hy-Vee is headquartered here, and Microsoft runs several data centers in the city.

People relocating for a job and heirs living in other states frequently want a fast closing rather than a house to look after remotely.

The West Des Moines Community School District covers most of the city, while the Dallas County portion falls under the Waukee Community School District.

Its schools include eight elementaries, two junior highs, Valley High School, Valley Southwoods (a freshman high school) and the Walnut Creek Campus, an alternative high school. The parcel record shows the district for a particular house.

Interstates 35, 80 and 235 all reach West Des Moines, and Iowa Highway 28 forms much of the boundary with Des Moines. Street numbers do not match Des Moines: Eighty-sixth Street in Clive becomes 22nd Street in West Des Moines. Buses come from Des Moines Area Regional Transit, and the mean commute is 18.3 minutes.

sections.h2: Flood risk, sump pumps and basements
sections.html:
The Raccoon River and Walnut Creek both have significant flood potential. After the Great Flood of 1993 a floodwall was built along Walnut Creek.

  • Clive, Des Moines and West Des Moines run the Des Moines Metro ALERT system, which uses rain and stream gauges to watch conditions and to operate the Raccoon River and Walnut Creek levee system.
  • A FEMA flood map is available for any address.
  • High groundwater often floods basements in spring, and owners are generally responsible for their sump pumps. Never connect a sump pump to the sanitary sewer.
  • Sanitary sewer backups can be reported to Public Services at 515-222-3480.

The January mean high is 26 degrees F and the July mean high is 86 degrees F. If your basement runs damp or the sump setup is old, buyers will ask.

The rule most likely to affect a sale is rental licensing. The Building Division inspects every rental every two years and issues the license, and a property the owner does not occupy counts as a rental even if non-owner relatives live in it.

  • After an inspection, owners are told what repairs are required and generally have 30 days to finish them.
  • The Rental Housing Certificate is issued once fees are paid and repairs are done. It lasts until the next inspection and passes to a new owner.
  • It can be revoked if new violations appear between inspections and are not fixed.

Building permits are requested through the City Access Portal. The Development Services Department is at 4200 Mills Civic Parkway, and the Building Inspection office can be reached at 515-222-3630 or bi@wdm.iowa.gov. Call that office to ask whether a sale triggers an inspection of the property.

sections.h2: Which county bills the property tax?
sections.html:
Your tax bill comes from the county holding the parcel: usually Polk, sometimes Dallas, Warren or Madison. Check the parcel record before planning a closing.

In Polk County a single statement goes out in late August. Half is due September 1 and half March 1, and 1.5 percent interest is added on the first of every month once the grace date passes. A postmark by the due date counts. The Polk County Treasurer's phone is 515-286-3060.

Warren County, which holds a small part of the city, set its fiscal 2027 county levy at 5.64659 per $1,000 of taxable value for urban property, down from 5.84267 the year before. At closing, taxes are normally prorated and the buyer is credited for the seller's share, which you can verify on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: Transfer tax and recording a deed
sections.html:
The transfer tax on real estate is 80 cents per $500 of value past the first $500, and Iowa Code 428A.3 puts the liability on the seller.

A taxable deed is not recorded until the recorder has collected the tax, and the deed travels with a declaration of value signed by buyer, seller or agent. Exemptions cover transfers without consideration: distributions to heirs, deeds to a lender in lieu of foreclosure, and transfers between spouses or between parent and child.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a West Des Moines house
sections.html:
Owners can list with an agent, sell alone, or sell to a cash buyer, and every route swaps time for effort in a different way.

  • List with an agent: your house gets marketed, though repairs, showings and the buyer's loan drive the timeline.
  • Sell it yourself: you manage the listing, the paperwork and the price conversation.
  • Cash buyer: as-is purchase with a closing date built around your plans.

Cash works for an inherited house, a rental whose certificate lapsed, or a property that needs work. Send the address and your situation, and a written offer comes back that you can turn down.

faqs.q: Is West Des Moines in Polk County or Dallas County?
faqs.a: Most of it is in Polk County. Parts extend into Dallas County, and small portions are in Warren and Madison counties, so the parcel record decides which county bills a given house.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a West Des Moines house?
faqs.a: Polk County bills half by September 1 and half by March 1. After the grace date, 1.5 percent interest is added monthly, and buyer and seller usually split the year at closing.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a West Des Moines rental?
faqs.a: The license must be current while the unit is rented. Inspections come every two years, and the Rental Housing Certificate passes to a new owner. Call 515-222-3630 to find out where yours stands.

faqs.q: Who pays Iowa transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: The seller. Under Iowa Code 428A.3 the person conveying the property owes it, at 80 cents per $500 beyond the first $500, with heir distributions exempt.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in West Des Moines that is in a flood area?
faqs.a: Yes. A FEMA flood map is available for any address, and buyers and lenders will look at it. Gather any past flood or sump pump information before you speak with buyers.
